criteria.reason: The full NEXT definition (lines 111-115, identical in both copies) is right: few steps, numbered, in order, one fenced block per slash command under its line, a non-command step on its own line. But the four-section template a few lines above it (line 71, both copies) still describes NEXT as 'the exact command or action, ready to run' -- the single-command framing this change replaces -- so the rule contradicts itself. Line 71 should describe NEXT as the steps to take now, in order.
Zero matches for 'literal next command' in both copies; both say 'never a menu' and 'never a shell command'.
Both copies say 'the few steps to take now (usually one to three)', which states the short-NEXT rule.

implement-trd NEXT template is ordered numbered steps with one fenced block per slash command; zero matches for 'single next command' / 'name ONE' in both copies (confirmed by the judge directly), and the .claude copy is identical.
verify-build O4 passage keeps the rule, lists commands as numbered steps, one fenced block each, and a merge or deploy that must come first leads as plain text; .claude copy identical.

No gh pr hits; remaining git add/commit lines are commits the commands run themselves (audit-build report commit and artifacts.json commit, close-feature close commit, implement-trd checkpoint); the error-table stash/commit hint is out of scope by owner ruling. NEXT says merge the PR in words, by number and URL, as its only step.
